Company Overview
ACS (Allen Control Systems) is a defense technology company building precision robotic systems for the United States and its allies. Founded by two former U.S. Navy electrical engineers with deep experience in robotics and software, ACS brings together AI, computer vision, precision motion, and advanced hardware to solve complex defense challenges across land, air, and maritime environments.

Our flagship product, Bullfrog, is an autonomous precision weapon system that transforms existing weapons into highly accurate counter-drone systems — giving warfighters a scalable, cost-effective response to one of the fastest-growing threats on the modern battlefield. Bullfrog is deployed with U.S. forces, and ACS works with organizations throughout the U.S. military and national security community.

Following a $200 million Series B at a $2.2 billion valuation, ACS is rapidly expanding manufacturing, accelerating Bullfrog deployments, and developing the next generation of autonomous battlefield systems. This is an opportunity to join a proven, fast-moving team and help scale technology with direct, real-world impact on national security.

ACS is headquartered in Austin, Texas, with additional operations in Alexandria, Virginia; Mountain View, California; and Huntsville, Alabama. For more information, visit allencontrolsystems.com http://allencontrolsystems.com.




About the Role

We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Supply Chain Intern to join our growing team. This internship provides hands-on experience across supply chain operations, including procurement, planning, supplier management, inventory, logistics, and data analysis.

The ideal candidate is eager to learn, comfortable working in a fast-paced manufacturing environment, and interested in understanding how materials and suppliers support production from start to finish. You will work closely with Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, and Operations teams while contributing to projects that directly support production and company growth.



What You’ll Do

 - Support day-to-day supply chain activities across procurement, planning, inventory, and supplier management.

 - Assist Buyers and Supply Chain team members with purchase orders, supplier follow-up, order tracking, and delivery status.

 - Communicate with suppliers regarding lead times, delivery schedules, order status, and other purchasing needs.

 - Help monitor material availability and identify potential shortages or risks that could impact production.

 - Assist with maintaining accurate supplier, purchasing, inventory, and material data within ERP/MRP systems.

 - Support inventory analysis, cycle counts, and inventory accuracy initiatives.

 - Collect and analyze supply chain data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement.

 - Help develop and maintain reports, trackers, dashboards, and supplier performance metrics.

 - Support supplier performance tracking related to quality, delivery, cost, and responsiveness.

 - Assist with sourcing activities, including supplier research, quote collection, and basic cost comparisons.

 - Support production planning and material readiness for upcoming builds.

 - Partner with Manufacturing and Engineering teams to understand changing material requirements and priorities.

 - Assist with new product introduction (NPI) and supply chain readiness for new or changing products.

 - Support continuous improvement projects focused on reducing lead times, improving material flow, increasing inventory accuracy, and strengthening supplier performance.

 - Participate in cross-functional meetings and communicate project updates, risks, and findings.

 - Take ownership of assigned projects and present results or recommendations to the Supply Chain team.



What We’re Looking For

 - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Business, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Data Analytics, or a related field.

 - Strong interest in supply chain, manufacturing, procurement, logistics, or operations.

 - Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

 - Comfortable working with data and identifying trends or discrepancies.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills.

 - Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams.

 - Self-motivated and comfortable taking ownership of assignments.

 - Ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and rapidly changing environment.

 - Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and other standard productivity tools.



Preferred Qualifications

 - Previous internship, co-op, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, inventory, or logistics experience.

 - Experience with Excel functions such as PivotTables, XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP, formulas, and data analysis.

 - Exposure to ERP/MRP systems such as Odoo, NetSuite, SAP, or similar.

 - Familiarity with purchasing, inventory management, production planning, or supplier management.

 - Experience creating reports, dashboards, or analyzing operational data.

 - Interest in manufacturing, robotics, aerospace, defense, automotive, or other hardware-focused industries.



What You’ll Gain

As a Supply Chain Intern, you will gain practical experience supporting a fast-moving manufacturing organization and learn how procurement, suppliers, inventory, planning, engineering, and production work together.

You will have the opportunity to work on meaningful projects, develop your analytical and problem-solving skills, interact directly with cross-functional teams, and gain exposure to the full supply chain lifecycle—from sourcing and purchasing through material delivery and production.

Robotics Engineering Intern
San Francisco · Onsite · Internship

About Bracket Bot

We believe planet earth can thrive and be alive. Robots should manufacture goods, clean roadways, tidy our rooms, build more homes, cook healthy food, and lower the cost of living. We aren’t quite there yet, robots are too expensive, too difficult to program, fragile, and unfriendly. Bracket Bot is changing that.

We believe that robots are currently in the ENIAC era and we are bringing them to the Macbook era. We believe in high performance engineering teams where everyone you work with is what you imagined Bell Labs employees to be like. Intelligent, scrappy, dedicated, kind.

At Bracket Bot, we have a few objectives. We are working to make the ideal role model of a company, one where everyone is at the top of their field, inventing new ways to solve the problems we face across mechanical, electrical, software, and machine learning. What does a company that creates entirely new ways that teams work together look like? A company that invents new materials for lighter weight actuators and structures? A company that creates and publishes new inverse kinematics algorithms for robots? A company that is thinking radically differently, and executing on another level.

In every field there are small teams who did something their peers had decided was impossible. The 10-second barrier in sprinting, or the eight engineers who left Motorola and made the 6502 for 10x lower cost than other chips at the time making the personal computer possible. SpaceX has landed the same rocket 36 times. Bracket Bot believes actuated, alive machines can be glorious, affordable, easy to use, and ubiquitous, and we are pulling that future forward.

Our products are a mirror of what we think about the world, on engineering & research, and what we think should be introduced into the world. In history, there are simply products that should exist, and only once created, are obvious in hindsight. Bracket Bot’s mission is to introduce as many of these products into the world as possible. We believe there are hundreds of these in the space of robotics. Across physical robot hardware, software and operating system; the infrastructure and distributed systems they connect to; the AI inference they run, both local and cloud, and so much more.

Our first product, Bracket Bot 1, exemplifies what a small team of highly talented people can do. At Bracket Bot, we genuinely believe 100x engineers exist, and a room full of them can create things that dozens of other companies have failed to do. We’ve brought to market a robot that is 10x lower cost than any other robot in its category, while out performing them on manipulation, autonomous navigation, speech interaction, and developer UX.

We’re backed by Fifty Years (Scott Phoenix), BoxGroup, SV Angel, Betaworks, Pace Capital, angels including Nat Friedman, Logan Kilpatrick (Google AI), Guillermo Rauch (Vercel) and others from Tesla AI, Physical Intelligence, and Markforged.

About the role

Robotics brings mechanical systems, electronics, software, and machine learning together. The fastest way to learn is to build, test, and debug the whole system.

We’re hiring a Robotics Engineering Intern to contribute to hands-on engineering projects with the Bracket Bot team. You’ll help build and improve robots, investigate failures, and take scoped projects from an idea to a tested result.

Your work will draw on your strengths while giving you exposure to the other disciplines that make a robot work.

What you’ll do

 - Build, integrate, and test robot hardware or software with the engineering team.

 - Help reproduce failures, collect useful measurements, and debug system behavior.

 - Develop prototypes, tools, or tests that support robot development.

 - Document results and communicate what worked, what failed, and what to try next.

 - Own a scoped engineering project through implementation and verification.

What we’re looking for

 - Hands-on engineering projects that show curiosity and follow-through.

 - A foundation in mechanical, electrical, software, or robotics engineering.

 - Willingness to build, measure, debug, and learn unfamiliar systems.

 - Clear communication and the ability to ask useful questions.

 - Care for the quality of your work and enthusiasm for physical robots.

Nice to have

 - Personal, university, lab, or competition robotics projects.

 - Experience with CAD, electronics, programming, or practical fabrication.

 - Experience building test tools or documenting technical projects.

Important notes

 - This is a hands-on internship based onsite in San Francisco.

 - We value evidence of things you’ve built and problems you’ve worked through.

 - You’ll collaborate closely with engineers on real robot development.

Bracket Bot is an equal opportunity employer. We’re building a diverse team and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

WHAT TO EXPECT

Heron Power is a startup company building cutting-edge power electronics for the 21st-century grid. We aim to debottleneck the growth of electricity generation and consumption with scalable, innovative, and less costly hardware solutions, accelerating the electrification of everything.

Our first focus goal is to build better converters (inverters & rectifiers) to connect large-scale renewables, storage, and loads to the grid. Heron Power’s leadership team is made up of seasoned veterans who have designed and shipped gigawatts of power conversion products over the past decade.

We understand that no one individual knows everything. We will all learn a lot together and from each other. We strive to build a collaborative, enriching environment conducive to personal, technical, and career growth. You can expect to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, driven by first principles engineering, solving difficult problems.




JOB OVERVIEW

As an Intern, Automation Controls Engineer, you will support the wiring, fabrication, and documentation of controls and automation equipment on our pilot production line and lab. Additionally, you will assist with sensor and field-device integration, PLC/HMI integration, and SOP creation, working closely with a controls engineer to ensure new work is integrated to an industry standard level.




HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE

 - Wire control panels, fabricate enclosures and brackets, and support mechanical build-out of automation equipment.

 - Specify, order, and install sensors and field devices (cables, junction boxes, labeling) to a consistent, production-ready standard.

 - Support PLC/HMI programming tasks under guidance, following existing naming conventions and documentation standards.

 - Read and red-line electrical schematics, and use tools such as Claude in PowerPoint/Excel to communicate scope of work.

 - Help document standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the pilot line and lab equipment.

 - Track task timelines and keep stakeholders informed of progress.




WHAT YOU WILL BRING




MUST-HAVE REQUIREMENTS

 - Organized, methodical work habits, with strong written documentation instincts.

 - Willingness to ask “what’s the best approach?” before building, rather than working in isolation.

 - Ability to follow and extend existing engineering conventions rather than starting from scratch.

 - Basic understanding of electrical/controls concepts (sensors, digital and analog I/O, wiring fundamentals).


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Sheet-metal or shop-class experience.

 - Exposure to PLC/HMI programming (e.g., basic sensor logic, ladder logic).

 - Schematic drafting experience (electrical or mechanical).

 - Experience sourcing industrial components (e.g., AutomationDirect).

 - Experience with HTTP/REST and other software APIs

If you are passionate about technology and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, we would love to hear from you. Join us in accelerating the electrification of everything at Heron Power.

Strong problem-solving and communication skills

Familiarity with GD&T and engineering drawing standards (ASME Y14.5)

From producing oil and gas to developing lower‑carbon technologies, Chevron engineers work across the full energy system to power everyday life more safely, efficiently, and responsibly. Learn more about What We Do and The Chevron Way.
Headquartered in Houston, Texas, Chevron operates around the globe and across the entire energy value chain. Learn more on our website Chevron.com.
What You’ll Actually Do
Chevron is hiring Facilities Engineering Interns for Electrical Engineering Intern roles at various operating locations across the U.S, including:
Ames, Iowa
Bakersfield, California
Belle Chasse, Louisiana
Covington, Louisiana
El Segundo, California
Geismar, Louisiana
Greeley, Colorado
Houston, Texas
Midland, Texas
Pasadena, Texas
Pascagoula, Mississippi
Richmond, California
Salt Lake City, Utah
Electrical, Instrumentation & Control Engineering interns will be assigned an engineering mentor and will be assigned one or more projects during their internship to support operating facilities through the application of technical engineering knowledge and project management skills. These areas of support may include:
Optimizing facilities to deliver maximum value safely and reliably.
Providing technical engineering support for turnarounds and projects.
Developing and/or deploying industry leading technologies to reduce carbon, increase efficiency and maximize returns.
Using digitalization and data analytics to improve process operations and safety.
At the completion of the internship, interns will have the opportunity to apply for a return internship or full-time position with Chevron. If accepted for a full-time entry level position, engineering graduates
will be enrolled in Chevron’s Horizons Program, an early-career development program combining formal training, on-the-job competency development, mentoring, and multiple job assignments. Electrical Engineers will be enrolled in either an Electrical Systems development track or an Instrumentation & Controls development path to develop a core technical foundation to draw upon throughout their career. Both tracks develop competencies for designing and maintaining instrumentation and control devices and electrical power systems and equipment, with specialization depending on the track assigned. Engineers in these roles support activities ranging from process control networks and process automation systems to optimize plants, operating large power systems and generators, assuring power system integrity and reliability, and monitoring power systems for efficient power management.
Horizons engineers typically complete the development program in their first five years of employment and may have the opportunity to work in multiple work locations during that time. After graduating from Horizons, mechanical engineers may continue to work in roles aligned with their initial Horizons track, or they may choose to focus on other areas of interest, including:
Reliability & Integrity Engineering – focused on asset integrity, reliability, maintainability, and operability of operating assets.
Technical Safety Engineering - identify hazards, assess risk, and develop mitigation strategies through application of engineering design principles to a managed level of risk for operating facilities and capital projects.

Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health

Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions

Position Summary:

Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.
As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.
3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:
Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
Contributing to positive patient experiences showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

Real Work, Real Impact – Tackle meaningful projects and gain insight into client services at a global investment firm

About Marvell
Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.
At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.
Your Team, Your Impact
Marvell’s Digital IC (or Digital Logic) Design teams span across multiple domains, giving you the opportunity to work on technologies that power next-generation cloud, AI, storage, and networking solutions. Some teams are responsible for the design and verification of high-performance Ethernet PHY chips. Other teams shape the micro-architecture of the blocks, accelerators and subsystems that make up a system-on-chip (SoC). Across all groups, you’ll collaborate with your direct team and cross-functional partners (across architecture, physical design, design verification, and more) to deliver robust, scalable solutions that enable Marvell’s leadership in data infrastructure.
What You Can Expect
Deep dive into the digital design and implementation of real chip design efforts
Develop and verify detailed, high-performance RTL design blocks and apply the digital design specifications for high-speed connectivity devices and next-generation chips
Conduct synthesis, static timing analysis, timing signoff, and power analysis
Debug design issues and ensure functional correctness
Investigate & execute new design techniques & flows, and explore emerging methodologies to improve design quality, efficiency, & productivity
Collaborate with chip architecture, design verification, & physical design teams to solve complex problems and contribute to a team building real products
What We're Looking For
Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 – Summer 2028
Completed courses focusing on circuit design, circuit theory, digital logic design, static timing analysis, computer architecture, Verilog, VLSI, digital signal processing (DSP), SoC/ASIC design, or electronics
Proficiency in programming & scripting languages like Python, Perl, Tcl
Experience using tools like Synopsys (Primetime), Cadence (Virtuoso & Spectre X), and Mentor
Hands-on experience with RTL design and a firm understanding on how it integrates into the overall ASIC design flow
Strong analysis, problem solving, and communication skills
Expected Base Pay Range (USD)
30 - 59, $ per hour.
The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.

Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. What you will be doing as an Indirect Procurement Area Intern:
An indirect procurement organization is the team that helps a company buy the goods and services it needs to operate, but that are not directly resold to customers. For example, in retail, indirect procurement may support areas like technology, facilities, equipment, marketing, travel, supplies, and maintenance. The team works with business partners to understand what they need, find qualified suppliers, negotiate pricing and contract terms, manage supplier relationships, and look for ways to reduce costs or improve service.
In simple terms, indirect procurement helps the company spend money wisely, choose the right suppliers, reduce risk, and make sure teams have what they need to run the business effectively.
As an intern, you will be responsible for sourcing a category of spend. For example, snow removal services, meat coat cleaning services, Microsoft services negotiations, etc.

The Regulated Bioanalytical Sciences team is advancing laboratory digital transformation by improving how assay workflows and experimental data are captured, structured, and managed within Benchling. Benchling serves as the Regulated Bioanalytical Sciences laboratory information management system used to capture, organize, and manage structured experimental workflows and data.
Activities may include reviewing Test Methods to identify workflow steps, data fields, and calculations, and translating those elements into structured Benchling templates supported by clear documentation. The project will help reduce manual template creation, improve consistency in experimental documentation, and future analytics readiness while reducing reliance on static TM documents.

Review prioritized Test Method documents to understand assay workflows, critical steps, documentation requirements, and data capture needs.
Translate TM content into standardized, reusable Benchling templates that support structured execution and documentation of laboratory workflows.

Collaborate with scientists and process owners to ensure templates accurately reflect method requirements and user needs.

The Opportunity:
We are seeking a proactive PhD Summer Intern to contribute to an exciting research project on our Corporate Functions R&D business. The project will be focused on developing and evaluating functional materials for various applications. This role involves assisting with the selection and integration of modifying agents, implementing chemical modification techniques, and characterizing the resulting materials for their physical and biological properties. A key component of the internship will be culturing bacteria and performing other microbiological assays, applying chemical techniques, and interpreting data to identify promising formulations. The intern will help provide recommendations for potential applications in areas such as consumer products, paper products, or textiles.
Key Responsibilities:
1. Production of Biopolymers with Pre-Defined, Integrated Functionality:
Successfully synthesize biopolymers where specific, desired functional groups (identified through literature search) are covalently incorporated into their chemical structure during bacterial fermentation. This results in a single-step, in-situ modification process. Produce functionally modified biopolymers using methods involving ex-situ chemical modification of pre-formed biopolymers.
2. Expanded Application Space for Biopolymers through Tailored Properties:
Create a diverse library of biopolymers exhibiting new or enhanced properties directly attributable to the incorporated functional groups and test them in the lab for efficacy (e.g., increased hydrophobicity/hydrophilicity, improved adhesion, enhanced biodegradability, antimicrobial activity, specific binding sites).
3. Based on 1. And 2. Make recommendations that provide the antimicrobial efficacy and beyond to allow application in spaces relevant to P&G
Job Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Education: Working towards a PhD in microbiology, chemical biology, polymer/material chemistry.
Microbiological Laboratory Proficiency: Skilled in aseptic technique, bacterial culturing, basic microbiological assays, and rigorous adherence to laboratory safety and best practices (chemical & biological).
Organic Synthesis & Reaction Skills: Proficient in setting up, running, and monitoring chemical reactions.
Agile R&D Contributor with Advanced Problem-Solving: Proactively drives project outcomes in dynamic lab environments by expertly analyzing results, identifying issues, and devising robust technical solutions and troubleshooting strategies across both chemical and microbiological contexts, while rapidly adapting to changes in project scope.
Available to work a 12-week internship from May/early June to August in the summer of 2027. 5 days a week in office at Mason Business Innovation Center location.
Preferred Skill Sets:
Chemical Characterization Techniques: Ability to perform and interpret data from techniques like FTIR, NMR, XRD.
Polymer Science Fundamentals: Understanding of polymer structure, properties, and how modifications affect material characteristics.

What You Get Out of the Internship​​
At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will: ​ ​
Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting​
Implement new ideas, be constantly challenged, and develop your skills​
Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business​
Be a part of an innovative team and culture​
Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format
Who we want​​
Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions.​
Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward.​
Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts.​
Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives.​
Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships.​
Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better.
Opportunities Available​
​As a Mechanical Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams:
Research & Development
New Product Development
R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products. They research new technologies, customer expectations, business requirements and regulations. They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts. These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production.
Product Engineering
R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products. They research new technologies, customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers. Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods. These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products.
Test Lab
Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process. What this really means is that we get to be the Mythbusters of our division. You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test. Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, we are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product. A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics. If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you!

Process Quality

Quality

Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process.  What this really means is that they get to be the MythBusters of the division.  You think your design can last the entire expected service life? As a Stores Executive Intern, you will get a valuable realistic preview of the Executive Team Leader role (Assistant Store Manager) over a defined period of time. Within this store management internship, you will work closely with other managers and team members to develop an understanding of how Target’s retail business works and what it takes to excel in a management role. You will be introduced to multiple areas of the store’s business, but the majority of your time will be spent leading amongst the team, identifying and working towards store priorities, and delivering great guest service.
This program is designed to teach individuals how to lead within a retail store and you will:
Learn how to drive guest experience and impact your store’s financial, team, and operational performance.
Work alongside a mentor and learn how they effectively lead their department within the store.
Have the opportunity to step into leading your mentor’s departments- of course, we will be there to guide you and help you learn along the way!
Spend your days learning to lead and motivate a team, drive sales results, merchandise products, and provide an exceptional experience for our guests.
Have ongoing development conversations, as your development will be a top priority of ours.
Lead and support the execution of daily operations by working with your team members to build culture and guide your team to grow and achieve goals.
Learn more from past Interns, Mentors, and Managers here.
At Target, we believe in our leaders having meaningful experiences that help them build and develop skills for a career. The goal of the Stores Executive internship is to provide a realistic job preview of an ETL role. The role of a Stores Executive Intern can provide you with the skills and experience of:
Guest service fundamentals and experience building and managing a guest-first team culture across the store
Guest engagement; problem-solving and resolution
Retail business fundamentals
Setting and planning department(s) monthly/quarterly workload to support business priorities and managing a team to deliver service and sales goals
Managing a team of hourly team members and team leaders while creating business strategies and goals
Recruiting, selecting and talent management of hourly team members and leaders
As a Stores Executive Intern, no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will most likely include the following responsibilities:
Spending time on the store salesfloor and backroom leading team members and aligning the team on daily business priorities
Working alongside your Executive Team Lead (ETL) mentor and other leaders in the building to gain an understanding of their roles
Leading through daily priorities (stocking shelves, ensuring a safe and welcoming environment that’s inviting to guests, helping build displays within the store, etc.)
Partnering with leaders regarding team member performance by teaching, coaching, training, and delivering timely performance feedback
Addressing team member concerns and removing hurdles to ensure smooth operations and goal attainment
Leading/presenting at daily huddles with peer/leadership team
Planning daily goals and organizing plans within the building
Providing summary of results and priorities with peer/leadership team
Working with store leaders each day to set goals and expectations
Reviewing business reporting and guest insights to understand, troubleshoot and follow up on opportunity areas.
Delivering an exceptional guest experience by ensuring team members are knowledgeable and empowered to make it right for guests
Providing new ideas and recommend solutions to business or team opportunities
Taking the initiative to learn how to be a Target leader by seeking out opportunities for growth and development; continuously learning throughout the internship experience
Commit to learning Target’s expectations of leaders and use them to personally develop by asking questions and seeking feedback
Actively participate in internship program training activities, developmental opportunities and events
Demonstrate a willingness to take strategic risks and take on new assignments
Demonstrate a culture of ethical conduct, safety, and compliance; lead the team to work in the same way and hold others accountable to this commitment
Work in a safe manner at all times to benefit yourself and others; identify and correct hazards; comply with all safety policies and best practices
Foster an inclusive, equitable, safe, and secure culture
Carry out principal duties and responsibilities by the department
Gain an understanding of all business areas to develop business acumen
Create a welcoming experience by greeting guests as you are completing your daily tasks.
When guests need assistance, engage with guests in a welcoming way, to help solve their specific needs
Thank guests and let them know we’re happy they chose to shop at Target
All other duties based on business needs
ALL ABOUT YOU
This may be the right job for you if:
You enjoy interacting and helping others - including guests that shop our store and fellow team members you work with.
You thrive in a fast-moving, highly active and physically demanding role, where teamwork, flexibility, and creative problem solving are key to success.
You are open to working a flexible work schedule with varying hours, days or shifts (including nights, weekends, holidays and other peak shopping times).
The good news is that we have some amazing training that will help teach you how to be an effective leader within our stores. But there are a few things you need from the get-go:
Previous retail experience preferred, but not required
Strong interest in working in retail, specifically within our stores in management
Leadership skills and team-oriented thinking
Learn and adapt to current technology needs
Work independently and as part of a team
Manage workload and prioritize tasks independently
Welcoming and helpful attitude
Effective communication skills
We are an awesome place to work and care about our teams, so we want to make sure we are clear on a few more basics that we expect:
Access all areas of the building to respond to guest or team member issues
Interpret instructions, reports, and information
Accurately handle cash register operations as needed
Climb up and down ladders as needed
Scan, handle and move merchandise efficiently and safely, including frequently lifting or moving merchandise up to 44 pounds
Ability to communicate on multiple frequency devices and operate handheld scanners, and other technology equipment as directed
Flexible work schedule (e.g., nights, weekends and holidays) and reliable and prompt attendance necessary

ALL ABOUT OUR SUPPLY CHAIN OPERATIONS INTERNSHIP
Experience firsthand what it’s like to lead a team within a Target Supply Chain Facility. This internship is a paid 40 hr./week, hands-on training program to develop and prepare for your operations leadership. As an Operations Intern, you’ll gain a realistic job preview into life as an Operations Manager over a defined period of time. Within this Operations Management internship, you will work closely with other managers and team members in the building to develop an understanding of how Target’s supply chain business works and what it takes to excel in a management role. You’ll lead and support the execution of daily operations by working beside your team members and learn to lead, motivate and influence a team, including the opportunity to lead a department.
This program is designed to teach individuals how to lead within a supply chain facility. You will work closely with a Mentor as you take a deeper dive into how they effectively lead their department while gaining a line of sight into different business areas and functions within the building. You will spend your days learning how to problem solve, lead and motivate a team, conduct real-time observations, and drive results, all while ensuring safety is a top priority and that we are maximizing productivity to get products to the guest as fast as possible. During your internship, you will have the opportunity to step into leading your Mentors work center - of course, we will be there to guide you and help you learn along the way! Your development will be a top priority of ours, and to ensure you’re feeling supported, you can expect ongoing developmental conversations with your Mentor and Manager. We’ll be supporting you with extensive training to help you grow as a strong operations intern.

Experience in building and managing a team culture across the building
Problem solving and change management skills
Knowledge of retail business fundamentals
Experience setting and planning department(s) daily/weekly workload to support business priorities and managing a team to deliver goals

Provide summary of results around plan attainment, share hurdles, successes, and key learnings to apply moving forward at end of shift.

Conduct safety walks in building to identify, resolve and report findings.
Conduct follow-ups on team member attendance, any necessary coaching, etc.

Provide new ideas and recommend solutions for business or team opportunities

Foster an inclusive, safe, and secure culture

Business Unit
What the Role Entails
With over 20 years of research and experience in audio and video technology, Tencent Cloud launched Tencent Cloud Media Service, a new international audio and video brand, in 2022. It provides a one-stop media solution, the basic media processing infrastructure named MPS, including industry-leading encoder, Media enhancement based on AI technology and cloud real-time rendering and transmission technology, etc. Tencent Cloud Media Service also provides complete live streaming solutions for different industries, including OTT, e-commerce, entertainment, e-sports, and sports events, etc. Through comprehensive audio and video SDKs and PaaS services. Overall, Tencent Cloud Media Service offers low-cost, efficient, and innovative solutions for the businesses of global customers.Work closely with the regional sales team as the point of contact for customers in the field of audio and video. Provide technical support for pre-sales technical consultation and PoC verification services, maintain customer relationships, and assist the business team in achieving their goals.
Support the regional architecture team in analyzing customers' media business technology architecture and identifying their needs and values in audio and video scenarios. Provide industry solutions and case studies for international markets, such as OTT, social media, gaming, education, and business.
Understand industry solutions and combine customers' business and technical requirements with the features of Tencent's audio and video products. Help customers achieve their goals and values. Effectively communicate the customer requirements and industry requirements to product development team.
Actively participate in public online and offline product/industry presentations to share Tencent's media product capabilities, industry experience, and insights. Enhance the influence of Tencent Cloud Media Service, strengthen and establish Tencent's industry customer network in the field of media services.
Actively collaborate with the channel and marketing teams to support Tencent Cloud's regional ecosystem partners, including channel empowerment training, participating in workshops, and Media Demo Day.
Who We Look For
Currently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Computer Science, IT, Cloud Computing, or a related field. Relevant coursework, projects, or internships in cloud computing are a plus.

Join the future of news
We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.
About Our Team
The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning Newsroom and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.
Why This Role Matters
The Washington Post is seeking college juniors, seniors and graduate students for the newsroom’s flagship summer internship program. Our interns report and write articles, edit copy, take photographs, shoot and edit video, create graphics, produce audio, design on multiple platforms, develop audience strategy and do data analyses. They work alongside and learn from award-winning journalists, and we treat them as staff members during their internship.
What Motivates You
You’re driven to capture the stories that inform, educate, inspire and delight audiences, using different formats and mediums.
You thrive in fast-moving environments and on deadline.
You are eager to work across a large, ambitious, collaborative newsroom.
How You’ll Support the Mission
You will work with reporters and editors on engaging, high-impact stories, including breaking news, insightful features and visually driven enterprise work.
Photo interns will shoot in the field, covering a wide range of subjects, from politics to lifestyle.
Video interns will shoot video for immersive storytelling projects and clip news video for use on our owned and operated platforms.
The Skills and Experience You Bring
You must be a college junior, senior or graduate student enrolled in a degree program by the application deadline, which is noon Eastern time on Friday, Oct. 9, 2026.
You are passionate about visual storytelling and its power to shape how audiences experience the news.
Photo interns must be proficient in Photoshop CS, photo management software, and Mac and PC platforms.
Video interns must be proficient in all aspects of digital video/audio and editing software, including Final Cut Pro or Adobe Premiere. Experience with voiceover narration and HTML is helpful.
You have a commitment to accuracy, clarity and journalistic rigor.
Applications should include a résumé, autobiographical essay (which should be no more than 500 words), and a portfolio that includes three examples of your work. Please include an explanation of your role in the clips. Cover letters are not required. Materials can be submitted as links or documents to the same field labeled Resume/Cover Letter/Work Samples.
The deadline to apply is noon Eastern on Friday, Oct. 9, 2026.
This position will be based out of our Washington, D.C., headquarters. Interns are paid $1021.13/week.
Your story awaits. Apply today!
Learn more about The Post at careers.washingtonpost.com.
